subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should this concurrent allow-always race be fixed through the broader guarded exec-approval write path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226, a narrower replacement for this issue, or a larger metadata-storage redesign?
rationale: All viable fixes touch the persisted host-exec approval security boundary and can change how stale writes interact with admin revocations, so automation should not open another branch until maintainers choose the write contract.

options.title: Adopt guarded core write path
options.body: Rework or replace the open CAS/locking PR so every allow-always and usage write reloads or verifies current approval state before saving.

options.title: Land a narrow race fix
options.body: Fix only concurrent allow-always entry loss with a lock/merge helper and leave broader metadata/admin-revocation races to the linked security issue.

options.title: Defer to storage redesign
options.body: Pause this bug fix until maintainers choose whether runtime usage metadata should move out of exec-approvals.json.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded core write path
recommendation.body: Rework or replace the open CAS/locking PR so every allow-always and usage write reloads or verifies current approval state before saving.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent approval-store and node policy-layer commits make this the strongest routing candidate for the persistence contract choice.
